factCheck.setBy: general-purpose fact-check agent (2026-11-09); 785.38 and 484.60 added after, verified by writer on Cornell LII

coldRead.icp: DON at a 25-bed rural hospital, reading once on a phone

undefinedTerms: discipline (as in 'which discipline each visit needs')
territory and mileage limits / configurable agency guardrails
personal care services vs. home health services (Medicaid)
Medicaid-funded visits (post never says how to tell if my agency has any)
42 CFR Part 484 / Part 485 Subpart F / 485.631(a)(5) / 42 U.S.C. 1396b(l) / Section 12006(a) of the Cures Act (cites with no plain-language consequence for me)
conditions of participation (used before HHA is spelled out)
same employer (is a hospital-run agency the same employer for overtime? never stated)
coverage rules set up with you at onboarding
a scheduling team checks it (who, what do they check)
service vs. software (used interchangeably for SimpleScheduleAI)
mondayActions: Make a list of every nurse who worked both home visits and inpatient shifts in the last month
For those nurses, add one recent week across both schedules and compare to overtime payroll actually paid
Call or email the state Medicaid program to ask which EVV system the agency must use
Ask any vendor whether it was built for visits or for shifts, and ask for a sample week of the side I care about
Stop expecting one product to cover both the agency and the inpatient unit
Know that EVV does not apply to inpatient shifts, so I do not need to chase it for the unit
blockedActions: Assign one person to check combined hours each week: no method, no report name, no sample sheet, no named owner (payroll? me? the agency manager?)
Add up one week across both schedules: the two schedules live in different systems and the post never says where the agency hours come from or what format to use
Compare to overtime payroll actually paid: does not say what I do if I find nurses already over 40 combined
Ask the state Medicaid program about EVV: does not say which office or who to contact, or how to find out whether my agency even has Medicaid patients
Treat agency and inpatient hours as one total: does not settle whether my agency is the same legal employer as the hospital, which decides whether the total applies
Ask each vendor for a sample week: does not say what a good one looks like
